analyzed_vuln.description: `unpack_hex` uses the template-derived `count` (an `int`) directly as the length argument to `mrb_str_new(mrb, NULL, count)` without validating overflow/negativity after parsing. For crafted large decimal counts in unpack format (e.g. `h3333339010`), `count` wraps to a negative value, then is converted to `mrb_int` in string creation. This leads to invalid embedded-string indexing in `str_init_embed` (`RSTR_EMBED_PTR(s)[len]`) and UB/OOB access.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From `mruby_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled Ruby source is executed. Calling `String#unpack` with a HEX directive (`h`/`H`) and an excessively large repeat count that overflows 32-bit signed `int` causes `read_tmpl`/template parsing to produce negative wrapped `count`. `pack_unpack` passes this to `unpack_hex`, which allocates output string with that negative length via `mrb_str_new`, triggering the crash path in `mruby/src/string.c` when embedded-string initialization uses the invalid length.
